UnitStatement: Validation Manual Skeleton (document title heading).
This manual organizes verification and validation evidence for OpenPipeStress software quality.
The manual does not certify a piping model, decide code compliance, authenticate a professional judgment, or approve project-specific reliance.
Current authority basis is execution/_Decomposition/SOFTWARE_DECOMP.md revision 0.7 and the approved execution/_DAG/DAG-006/ graph coordination authority.

DAG-006 supplies active dependency context only; it does not settle lifecycle state, release labels, legal clearance, professional approval, certification, sealing, authentication, or code-compliance claims.
The manual answers four separate questions, each with its own evidence class and decision owner.
Mechanics verification answers whether the software matches a declared mechanics problem within a declared tolerance; decision owner is maintainers using recorded benchmark evidence.
Workflow validation answers whether the workflow preserves assumptions, warnings, reproducibility, and user-facing limitations; decision owners are maintainers and reviewers.
User rule check answers whether a user-supplied rule pack ran deterministically against its stated inputs; decision owner is the user or project authority.
Professional reliance context answers whether a real project calculation is acceptable for reliance; decision owner is a competent human reviewer.
Software evidence can support the reliance question but cannot replace human review of model scope, inputs, assumptions, rule basis, limitations, and reporting context.
State PLANNED means the section exists but no accepted evidence is recorded.
State DRAFT_EVIDENCE means evidence exists but thresholds, provenance, review, or repeatability remain incomplete.
State MAINTAINER_REVIEWED means maintainers reviewed the evidence for software-quality use.
State BLOCKED means required evidence cannot be used until a source, provenance, licensing, or technical issue is resolved.
State TBD means a governed decision or evidence record is still missing.
Final release thresholds, public benchmark acceptance, release labels, and professional reliance wording remain TBD unless a human governance record says otherwise.
GUI validation evidence requirements and validation evidence-bundle storage also remain TBD.

Product scope and limitations section is professional reliance context, sourced from docs/PROFESSIONAL_BOUNDARY.md and docs/IP_AND_DATA_BOUNDARY.md, covering intended support role, exclusions, private-data boundary, reliance warning, and known unsupported cases.

Solver theory summary section is verification context, sourced from docs/theory/centerline_analysis.md and solver docs, covering stated mechanics assumptions, element families, load handling, nonlinear support limits, and result-envelope policy.

Unit and schema verification section is mechanics verification, sourced from schema tests, core/units/, and docs/TYPES.md, covering unit dimensions, schema validation, invalid-input behavior, and serialization boundaries.
Element verification section is mechanics verification, sourced from validation/benchmarks/mechanics/, covering frame, straight-pipe, support, thermal, imposed displacement, and transform benchmarks.

Load and stress recovery verification section is mechanics verification, sourced from validation/benchmarks/stress/ and load and stress modules, covering axial, bending, torsion, pressure membrane, stress range, load-case algebra, and documented tolerances.

Nonlinear support verification section is mechanics verification, sourced from validation/benchmarks/nonlinear/, covering active-set behavior, gap/lift-off/friction cases, and convergence and non-convergence diagnostics.

Rule-pack evaluator verification section is user rule check, sourced from rule schemas, evaluator tests, and invented rule packs, covering required inputs, unit awareness, sandboxing, deterministic pass/fail status, and checksum/provenance.

GUI workflow validation section is workflow validation, sourced from GUI workflow tests and screenshots when available, covering missing-data behavior, warning visibility, assumptions, solve status, and result state transitions.

Report reproducibility validation section is workflow validation, sourced from report generator, audit manifest, and protected-content linter, covering stable output, checksums, warning inclusion, provenance disclosure, and professional-boundary notice.

Known limitations and open issues section is cross-cutting, sourced from issue records, release notes, and the TBD queue, covering missing evidence, unapproved thresholds, source restrictions, model limitations, and accepted risks.
Mechanics benchmarks (validation/benchmarks/mechanics/, validation/hand_calcs/mechanics/) are DRAFT_EVIDENCE; final public benchmark acceptance and release tolerances are TBD.
Stress recovery benchmarks (validation/benchmarks/stress/, validation/hand_calcs/stress/) are DRAFT_EVIDENCE; fatigue, allowable, and release-threshold decisions are TBD.
Nonlinear support regression (validation/benchmarks/nonlinear/) is DRAFT_EVIDENCE; production release thresholds and external validation claims are TBD.
GUI workflow validation evidence is PLANNED; required evidence type, coverage, and review criteria are TBD.

Report protected-content lint (core/reporting/protected_content_linter/) provides draft review evidence for report and public-artifact checks but does not provide legal clearance, professional approval, or code-compliance proof.
Release quality evidence (future DEL-09-05 release quality gate checklist) is TBD; the manual may organize evidence inputs but does not settle release labels or release readiness.
Validation evidence bundles (future evidence package location/format) are TBD; long-term storage, retention, and release attachment policy are unsettled.
Professional boundary (docs/PROFESSIONAL_BOUNDARY.md) is a draft policy surface for reliance wording and release-claim limits.
This inventory is not complete validation, release readiness, legal clearance, or professional reliance evidence; it is the starting index for future evidence review and release-quality decisions.
Each manual section must include its purpose and evidence class.
Each manual section must include the source artifacts and commands used to generate evidence.
Each manual section must include expected behavior and comparison basis.
Each manual section must include the tolerance or threshold source, or TBD if not governed.
Each manual section must include provenance and redistribution status for public examples.
Each manual section must include known limitations and excluded interpretations.
Each manual section must include review disposition and open risks.
A formal hand-calc witness is a machine-readable validation evidence artifact.

A hand-calc witness records the problem statement, assumptions, units, symbolic relations, numeric inputs, intermediate quantities, expected results, tolerances or TBD tolerance markers, provenance, redistribution status, and review disposition.
The machine-readable witness artifact is authoritative for automated comparison, hashing, reproducibility, and review traceability.
Markdown, MathML, PDF, or other human-facing hand-calc pages are deterministic renderings generated from the witness artifact.
Human-facing renderings support inspection and review but are not the source of record when they disagree with the machine-readable witness.
Hand-calc witnesses must remain limited to open mechanics, invented or cleared public evidence, and user-supplied private data where applicable.

Hand-calc witnesses must not embed protected standards text, protected tables, proprietary benchmark files, private rule-pack content, code-specific acceptance criteria, or any statement that the software certifies, seals, approves, authenticates, or declares code compliance for project reliance.
Public validation examples must be original, public-domain, or permissively licensed.

Public artifacts must not copy protected standards text, protected tables, protected examples, proprietary commercial benchmark files, private owner data, private user models, or vendor data without documented rights.
Private rule packs, private material libraries, owner requirements, and project models belong in user-controlled project records.
Private records may be referenced in a private validation package but must not be copied into public OpenPipeStress artifacts.
Before a manual section is treated as maintainer-reviewed software evidence, reviewers perform a defined set of checks.
Reviewers check that evidence commands and inputs are recorded.
Reviewers check that expected results are reproducible from repository artifacts or documented external sources with redistribution rights.
Reviewers check that generated hand-calc renderings trace back to their authoritative machine-readable witness artifacts.
Reviewers check that units and assumptions are explicit.
Reviewers check that warnings, non-convergence, and missing-data behavior are not collapsed into a generic success state.
Reviewers check that protected-content and private-data scans are clean or risk-dispositioned.
Reviewers check that professional reliance wording stays human-owned.
Reviewers check that unresolved gaps remain visible as TBD or open issues.
